# A header menu's late search focus pulls focus off the value just picked

> **Correction (2026-10-21, before the PR):** this body first presented the race below as the cause of the `#19928` arm's `e2e-engine` flake. The race is real: a held-focus e2e shows it deterministically, red on base and green with the fix. But it is not the arm's only cause. Under the same conditions, the arm still failed 2 of 16 runs at head and 1 of 16 on base, with the same symptom. AC-3 is narrowed accordingly, and the arm's remaining cause is out of scope here.

## Context

The `#19928` arm in `test/playwright/e2e/grid/IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs` ("the filter list draws its focus ring inside the row and its rows on the menu surface, in both themes") fails intermittently in `e2e-engine (3/4)`. It failed on the first runs of #19958 and #19960: `.neo-navigator-active-item` is not found after a pick. @neo-gemini-maryam traced one mechanism (A2A, 2026-10-21): a late search focus that pulls focus off the value just picked.

## The Problem

Opening a header menu focuses its search field one worker↔main round trip after the surface shows. Two calls did it: `Menu#open()` explicitly, and the floating container's own `focusOnMount` (`Component#afterSetMounted` pushes focus to the first focusable child). A pointer that picks a value inside that window gets focus first. The late focus then moves it to the search field, and `Neo.main.addon.Navigator` removes `.neo-navigator-active-item` on `focusout`. The pick still applies, but the active state the user just set is gone.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/header/plugin/Menu.mjs#open()`: `this.surface.hidden = false; await this.surface.promiseUpdate();` then the search focus. The surface also kept the floating default `focusOnMount: true`.
- `src/main/addon/Navigator.mjs` adds the active-item class on `focusin` and removes it on `focusout`.
- A worker-side guard such as `surface.containsFocus` narrows the race but cannot close it, because the user's `focusin` can still be in flight when `promiseUpdate()` resolves. The decision belongs on the main thread, at the moment the focus call lands.
- **Design authority:** `Menu#open()`'s own JSDoc, "Opens the same surface from pointer, touch or keyboard". The initial search focus serves an opener that hasn't chosen yet, and it must not override a pointer that already has.

## The Fix

- `DomAccess.focus` gains `unlessFocusWithin`: the id of a container whose current focus wins.
- `Menu#open()` becomes the surface's single focus owner: the surface sets `focusOnMount: false`, and `open()` focuses the search input with `unlessFocusWithin: surface.id`.
- Opening with no intervening pick keeps today's search focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A value picked right after opening, before the menu's search focus would land, keeps focus and its active-item state.
- [ ] AC-2: Opening without a pick still focuses the search field, so the keyboard path is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-3: A browser e2e drives the pick inside that window deterministically, by holding the menu's focus call on the main thread, and is red on base and green at head.

## Out of Scope

- The `#19928` arm's remaining flake. Another cause produces the same symptom; my earlier hypothesis is a click that lands before the Navigator's listeners re-bind after the theme switch.
- The same mount-focus race for other floating components (noted separately).
- #19955, #19953 and #19954.
